channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Braskem Debt Talks Drag on With No Deal Days Ahead of Deadline
item.description: Braskem SA said talks with creditors have intensified, but have yet to produce an agreement, with a deadline on a court-ordered shield from enforcement actions set to expire in just three days.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo

item.title: South African Rand Gains Below 16 Per Dollar, Erasing War Losses
item.description: South Africa’s rand strengthened below 16 per dollar, erasing its Iran war losses.
item.dc:creator: Mpho Hlakudi

item.title: Global Crude Refining Has No Margin for Error, Says Rapidan’s McNally
item.description: Bob McNally, founder and president at Rapidan Energy Group, examines pressure on the global crude refining system from increased Ukrainian attacks on Russia refiners and US facilities running at near maximum capacity following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Buyback Pledge Draws Japan Comparisons and Pressures Dollar
item.description: The US bond buyback pledge that whipsawed markets this week is prompting comparisons with policies in Japan, where efforts to contain borrowing costs resulted in prolonged currency weakness.
item.dc:creator: Vassilis Karamanis and Alice Gledhill

item.title: Treasuries Steady; Samsung's Shareholder Return Plans | Bloomberg Brief 08/21/2026
item.description: US equity futures rise, the dollar weakens, and bitcoin heads for its best week in more than three years as investors assess a potential for bigger US debt buybacks. Samsung Electronics plans to return as much as $80 billion to its shareholders this year. Max Kettner of HSBC discusses the implications of the underlying fiscal pressures in the US and looks ahead to Jackson Hole next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Expects to Match or Top SpaceX’s Record IPO Size | The Opening Trade 8/21/2026
item.description:
Anthropic expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX’s record-setting initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, in the latest sign of overwhelming demand from investors looking to profit from the artificial intelligence boom.
The Claude developer is running the numbers as it prepares to file publicly for its potential mega-IPO as soon as the end of this month, the people said. Recent investor briefings led by Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao skirted the question of valuation, they said.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Guy Johnson, Skylar Montgomery and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: German Manufacturing Boost, French Businesses Hit By Heatwave | The Pulse 8/21/2026
item.description:
"The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.
Today's guests: Modupe Adegbembo, Jefferies, Economist; Marina Zavolock, Morgan Stanley, Chief European Equity Strategist; Majid Jafar, Crescent Petroleum CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MLB Labor Dispute Drives Record Short Interest in Braves Stock
item.description: Short sellers are rapidly upping their bets against shares of the Atlanta Braves as contentious labor negotiations between Major League Baseball and its players union raise the prospects of a disruption to the 2027 season.
item.dc:creator: Norah Rami

item.title: US Stock Futures Gain as Nasdaq 100 Looks to Snap Five-Day Slump
item.description: US stock futures rose in early trading Friday, putting the Nasdaq 100 on track to end a five-day losing streak as bond yields stabilize and Bitcoin soars.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: India’s Nuclear Opening Comes With a High Security Bar
item.description: Investors seeking entry to the country’s atomic power sector will likely face scrutiny in one area above all others – their ability to safeguard critical infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Kumar Singh

item.title: Week of Whiplash in Treasuries Is Closing With Traders on Pause
item.description: After a turbulent stretch for the US bond market, traders are heading into Friday’s session with questions about what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s next move will be.
item.dc:creator: Alice Gledhill and George Nixon

item.title: Everybody’s Business: Are We Headed For Stagflation?
item.description: The Roosevelt Island Tram is a monument to the 1970s stagflation era when New York City ran out of money and couldn't borrow any more to build a subway between Manhattan and the island in the East River. On this episode of Everybody's Business, Stacey Vanek Smith and Allison Schrager ride the tram and talk stagflation: what is it and are we headed in that direction again? Listen to the full episode wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Turns Sour on Once-Buzzy Space Stock After 73% Rout
item.description: Wall Street analysts are rushing to slash their price targets on spacecraft and satellites manufacturer York Space Systems Inc., saying the company’s path forward looks uncertain amid supply chain troubles and a slower pace of government contracts.
item.dc:creator: Arvelisse Bonilla Ramos

item.title: Negative Economic Surprises Could Help Treasuries, HSBC’s Kettner Says
item.description: Max Kettner, chief multi-asset strategist at HSBC, sees US growth momentum starting to slow down and says, “a streak of a couple of weeks uninterrupted of negative economic surprises” can bring back a bid for duration in US Treasuries. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hua Hong, Weichai Power to Join Hong Kong’s Stock Benchmark
item.description: Hang Seng Indexes Co. is adding Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor Ltd. and Weichai Power Co. to Hong Kong’s equity benchmark, the index compiler said following its quarterly review.
item.dc:creator: Elaine Lai

item.title: Euro-Zone Business Activity Sees Surprise Improvement
item.description: Private-sector activity in the euro area unexpectedly improved slightly in August, thanks to the strongest manufacturing growth in more than four years. Bloomberg's Zoe Schneeweiss reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Post-Strike Movie Supply is Driving Theatre Demand, Vue Entertainment CEO says
item.description: Vue Entertainment CEO Tim Richards says the chain may see its strongest summer box office since the pandemic. "What we are seeing this year is all the movies in the post-strike period now hitting our screens. But we are also seeing the studios and content-makers producing and releasing movies at unprecedented levels." He speaks to Bloomberg's Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie, and Skylar Montgomery Koning. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Set for Third Weekly Gain on US Treasury Buyback Plans
item.description: Gold was on track for a third weekly advance after the US Treasury’s unexpected ramp-up in buybacks of long-dated government debt underscored concerns about its fiscal burden.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie and Jack Ryan

item.title: Stocks Rise as Bitcoin Rally Lifts Crypto Shares: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equities advanced, with crypto-linked stocks among the biggest gainers as Bitcoin headed for its best week in more than three years. Treasuries trimmed early gains as oil fluctuated.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren and Sagarika Jaisinghani

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 21
item.description: Oil headed for a significant weekly increase as traders awaited details on a US campaign to isolate Iran’s economy, with no apparent end in sight to a conflict that has slashed Middle East exports.
item.dc:creator: Rong Wei Neo and Grant Smith
